sections.title: Number Building & The Teen vs. Ty Contrast
sections.content:
Counting in English follows regular building blocks after 20:
- **21 to 99**: Combine the tens word with the unit word separated by a **hyphen (-)**: *twenty-one, thirty-five, forty-eight, ninety-nine*.

### The Critical Pronunciation Difference: -teen vs. -ty
Many English learners confuse **13-19** with **30-90**. The difference is in **word stress**:
- **-teen numbers (13, 14, 15)**: Stress is on the **SECOND syllable** and the vowel is long /iË / (*thir-TEEN*, *four-TEEN*).
- **-ty numbers (30, 40, 50)**: Stress is on the **FIRST syllable** and the ending is short /ti/ (*THIR-ty*, *FOR-ty*).

### Spelling Watch: 40 vs. 14
Notice: **fourteen** has a 'u', but **forty** drops the 'u' (F-O-R-T-Y)!

callouts.title: Hyphen Rule for Compound Numbers
callouts.text: Always put a hyphen between tens and ones: **twenty-one**, **fifty-five**, **ninety-nine**.

callouts.title: Spelling of Forty
callouts.text: 'Forty' is the only number whose spelling drops the 'u': four (4), fourteen (14), but **forty (40)**.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Compound numbers 21-99 take a hyphen (twenty-one, forty-five, ninety-nine).
Distinguish -teen (stress on 2nd syllable) from -ty (stress on 1st syllable).
Remember forty is spelled WITHOUT 'u' (forty, NOT fourty).
In phone numbers and room numbers, 0 is often read as 'oh'.
State age with 'is [number] years old' or simply 'is [number]'.
